title: AND of literal gates has a width-$l$ CNF
statement: Fix natural numbers $m$, $n$, and $l$, and let $g_0, \dots, g_{m-1}$ be Boolean functions of an input $x : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \{0,1\}$, one for each index $i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,m$, such that each $g_i$ is computed both by some DNF of width at most $l$ and by some CNF of width at most $l$. Let the circuits $c \in cs$ each be a single literal over the variables $0, \dots, m-1$, and let $C$ be the AND gate whose children are exactly these literals, evaluated on an input $x$ by substituting the value $g_i(x)$ for the $i$-th variable. Then the Boolean function computed in this way — the conjunction of the literal values $g_i(x)$ or their negations — is itself represented by a CNF $\psi$ of width at most $l$, in the sense that $\psi$ evaluates to $C$'s value on every input $x$.
hypotheses_covered: every child circuit in cs is a literal
each gate function has a DNF of width at most l
each gate function has a CNF of width at most l
the node is an AND node evaluated by substituting gate values for variables
replaced:
Consider an AND node $\mathrm{Circuit.node}\,\mathrm{true}\,cs$ whose children are all
literals, where each gate function has a width-$l$ DNF and a width-$l$ CNF
representation. Then the function computed by the node has a width-$l$ CNF $\psi$ with
$\mathrm{CNF.eval}\,\psi\,x = (\mathrm{Circuit.node}\,\mathrm{true}\,cs).\mathrm{eval}\,(\lambda i,\ \mathrm{gates}\,i\,x)$ for all $x$.
